cards.text: New king in Jerusalem, friend! Hezekiah is twenty-five years old when he takes the throne, and he reigns twenty-nine years. And here's the best news: he does what's right in the eyes of the LORD, just as King David, his ancestor, had done.

cards.question: In the first month of his very first year, King Hezekiah heads to the house of the LORD. What does he do with its doors?

cards.text: Then he brings in the priests and Levites and gathers them in the square on the east side. Friend, when the new boss calls a meeting in his first month, EVERYBODY knows a speech is coming.

cards.question: Hezekiah tells the Levites to consecrate themselves and the house of the LORD, and to remove from the Holy Place every ___.

cards.text: Then he tells them why. Our fathers were unfaithful, he says, and they turned their backs on the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: When the fathers shut the doors of the portico, they still kept the lamps burning.

cards.text: No incense, no burnt offerings in the Holy Place, doors shut, lights out. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a closed drawer, and I know that kind of dark.

cards.question: True or false: Hezekiah tells the Levites that the wrath of the LORD has fallen on Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.text: Heavy news, friend. He says this is why their fathers have fallen by the sword, and their sons, daughters and wives are in captivity.

cards.question: So what's in Hezekiah's heart to do, so the LORD's fierce anger will turn away from them?

answers.text: Make a covenant with the LORD
Send gifts to the king of Assyria
Lead the army out against Edom

cards.question: Hezekiah calls the Levites "my sons" and tells them not to be negligent. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD has chosen them to serve Him
The king will reward them with land
The people will judge them harshly

cards.text: Then the Levites set to work, and the text names fourteen of them, two from each of seven families. Kohathites, Merarites, Gershonites and more: it's a full roll call.

cards.question: They gather their brothers, consecrate themselves and go in to cleanse the house of the LORD, according to the command of the ___ by the words of the LORD.

cards.text: The priests go inside and bring out to the courtyard all the unclean things they find. Friend, for years I dreaded the day somebody cleaned out my drawer, but THIS cleanout? This one's beautiful.

cards.question: The unclean things from the temple are piled in the courtyard. Where do the Levites carry them?

answers.text: Out to the Valley of Elah

cards.question: The cleansing starts on the first day of the first month. They reach the portico on the eighth day, spend eight more days on the house itself, and finish on day ___.

cards.text: Then they report to King Hezekiah that the entire house of the LORD is cleansed, right down to the altar of burnt offering and the table of the showbread. The WHOLE house in sixteen days, friend, and I once spent an entire afternoon scrubbing ONE cookie sheet and bragged about it for a week.

cards.question: True or false: The articles that King Ahaz, the king before Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 28:27), cast aside in his unfaithfulness are now prepared, consecrated and set in front of the altar of the LORD.

cards.text: Early the next morning, King Hezekiah does NOT hit snooze. He gathers the city officials and goes up to the house of the LORD.

cards.question: They bring bulls, rams, lambs and male goats as a sin offering. How many of each?

cards.text: The king commands the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD. They slaughter the bulls, then the rams, then the lambs.

cards.question: After the bulls, the rams and the lambs are slaughtered, the priests splatter their ___ on the altar.
Next, the goats for the sin offering are brought before the king and the assembly. What do the king and the assembly do?

answers.text: Lead them out of the city

cards.question: The priests slaughter the goats and put their blood on the altar to make atonement. Who is the atonement for?

cards.text: Then Hezekiah stations the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps and lyres, by the command of David, of Gad the king's seer, and of Nathan the prophet. The Levites stand with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

cards.question: The command about the Levites and their instruments came from the LORD through His ___.
Hezekiah orders the burnt offering to begin. True or false: The song of the LORD and the trumpets wait until the offering is finished.

cards.text: The whole assembly is worshiping, the singers are singing and the trumpeters are playing, all the way until the burnt offering is completed. Friend, the loudest thing in my old drawer was the dead batteries arguing over who had charge left, so THIS? This is a SOUND.

cards.question: The offerings are completed. What do the king and everyone with him do next?

answers.text: Read the Book of the Law

cards.question: Hezekiah and his officials order the Levites to sing praises in the words of David and of Asaph the seer. True or false: The Levites sing them with gladness.

cards.text: Then Hezekiah says, "Now that you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD, come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD."

cards.question: The assembly brings sacrifices and thank offerings, and all whose ___ were willing bring burnt offerings.

cards.text: And the offerings pile UP: seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs for burnt offerings, plus six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep as consecrated offerings. Friend, back in the Millers' kitchen I thought a birthday batch was a big order.

cards.question: There aren't enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings, so their ___ brothers help them until the work is finished.
True or false: The text says the priests had been more diligent in consecrating themselves than the Levites.

cards.text: The Levites were the ready ones, and friend, I've been the one with the apron still untied when the timer goes off. The burnt offerings are abundant, and so the service of the house of the LORD is established.

cards.question: Hezekiah and all the people rejoice at what God had prepared for the people. Why?

answers.text: The enemy armies had gone home
The king had paid for all of it

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend. We're stopping here for now, but Hezekiah's story is NOT done.
